era: Game Boy through modern action RPG
summary: Square and Square Enix's action-RPG series, beginning as Final Fantasy Adventure and later spanning mainline console games, remakes, collections, DS spin-offs, and mobile entries.

entries.title: Final Fantasy Adventure

emulation.emulator: SameBoy for original Game Boy comparison
emulation.notes: Use the Switch collection for the main original-version route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official Switch collection output for the original Game Boy version.

primary.why: For the original 1991 game, Collection of Mana is the current official console route and keeps Final Fantasy Adventure in its original form alongside the first Mana trilogy.
primary.how_to_play: Play Collection of Mana on Nintendo Switch and select Final Fantasy Adventure. Use Game Boy hardware or a legally dumped ROM in SameBoy only for original-hardware comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not substitute the later remakes if the goal is the 1991 Game Boy design.

entries.title: Secret of Mana

emulation.notes: Use Collection of Mana for the main original-version run.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official Switch collection output for the original SNES version.

primary.version: Collection of Mana original SNES version
primary.why: For the original 2D Secret of Mana, Collection of Mana is the clean current official route while the 2018 3D remake is treated as its own entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play Collection of Mana on Nintendo Switch and select Secret of Mana. Use bsnes or original SNES hardware only for original-hardware comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: The original and 2018 remake are intentionally separate rows in this archive.

entries.title: Trials of Mana

emulation.notes: Use Collection of Mana for the main original-version run.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official Switch collection output for the original Super Famicom version.

primary.version: Collection of Mana original Super Famicom version
primary.why: For the original 1995 game, Collection of Mana supplies the official localized original version. The 2020 3D remake is handled as a separate entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play Collection of Mana on Nintendo Switch and select Trials of Mana. Use bsnes with a legally dumped Super Famicom cartridge only for original-release comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use the separate Trials of Mana (2020 remake) entry for the full 3D remake.

entries.title: Legend of Mana

emulation.notes: Use native Windows remaster for the main run.

primary.why: The remastered edition adds remastered visuals, soundtrack options, encounter toggle, and the Ring Ring Land mini-game; Windows is the best capture/settings route among current platforms.
primary.how_to_play: Play the remastered Legend of Mana on Steam or Windows Store. Use DuckStation only to compare the original PlayStation release.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original PlayStation look is different; use DuckStation only if preserving PS1 presentation matters.

entries.title: Sword of Mana

emulation.notes: Use clean scaling and original aspect ratio for capture.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: GBA emulation with LCD shader or clean pixel scaling.

primary.version: Original Game Boy Advance release via mGBA
primary.why: Sword of Mana is a distinct enhanced remake of Final Fantasy Adventure with expanded story, revised gameplay, and two protagonist routes, and it only shipped on Game Boy Advance.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped GBA cartridge in mGBA with integer scaling, or play on original GBA/DS hardware.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not a simple port of Final Fantasy Adventure; it changes plot and gameplay enough to deserve its own row.

emulation.notes: Use legal cartridge dumps; choose a layout that keeps the action screen readable for stream capture.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native DS rendering with clean scaling.

primary.version: Original Nintendo DS release via melonDS
primary.why: Children of Mana is a DS-only World of Mana dungeon-crawler spin-off; DS emulation gives the cleanest capture route while preserving the dual-screen layout.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped DS cartridge image in melonDS with a side-by-side screen layout, or play on original DS/3DS hardware.

entries.title: Friends of Mana

emulation.notes: No standard public emulator route is documented for a complete legal playthrough.

primary.why: Friends of Mana was a Japan-only multiplayer mobile RPG in the World of Mana project, so the original mobile service is the only version to document.
primary.how_to_play: No current official play route is documented; treat this as a preservation/history entry unless an official rerelease appears.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online/mobile availability is the main caveat; this is documented as historical coverage, not a current recommendation.

emulation.notes: Use legal disc dumps; test widescreen patches before committing to capture.

primary.why: Dawn of Mana is a PS2-only mainline Mana entry; PCSX2 upscaling is the highest-fidelity way to capture the original release.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped PS2 disc image in PCSX2 with 4x or higher internal resolution and widescreen only if verified safe for the game.

emulation.notes: Use legal cartridge dumps and a stable dual-screen layout.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native DS rendering with clean scaling.

primary.version: Original Nintendo DS release via melonDS
primary.why: Heroes of Mana is a DS-only real-time strategy entry and the sole release is best captured through DS emulation.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped DS cartridge image in melonDS with a readable dual-screen stream layout, or original DS/3DS hardware.

entries.title: Circle of Mana

emulation.notes: No complete public emulation route is documented.

primary.why: Circle of Mana was a Japan-only card-battle game for the GREE mobile platform, with no alternate release documented.
primary.how_to_play: No current official play route is documented after the original mobile/social release; treat as a historical archive entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Documented as historical coverage because the original social-game route is not currently available.

entries.title: Rise of Mana

emulation.notes: No complete legal offline route is documented.

primary.why: Rise of Mana shipped on iOS, Android, and PlayStation Vita, but the Vita version is the highest-fidelity/control-friendly historical route; all versions were discontinued in 2016.
primary.how_to_play: No current official play route is documented after service ended. If preserved legally, prefer the Vita version for physical controls and capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: Service ended in 2016, so this is not a current-play recommendation.

entries.title: Adventures of Mana

emulation.emulator: Vita3K not recommended as the main route
emulation.notes: Use owned Vita hardware or mobile; Vita emulation compatibility should be verified before capture.

primary.why: Adventures of Mana is a 3D remake of Final Fantasy Adventure; the Vita version keeps the remake on dedicated controls while mobile remains available as a touch-screen route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation Vita version if owned, or the mobile release on iOS/Android if current availability matters more than physical controls.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a remake of Final Fantasy Adventure, not a replacement for the 1991 original entry.

entries.title: Collection of Mana

primary.why: Collection of Mana is the official Switch anthology containing Final Fantasy Adventure, Secret of Mana, and the original Trials of Mana localization.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo Switch when you want the official original-trilogy package; use the individual game entries for the best route to each specific title.

entries.remaster_caveats: Collection contents are original-version routes, not the later 3D remakes.

entries.title: Secret of Mana HD

primary.why: The 2018 Secret of Mana remake rebuilds the game in 3D; Windows/Steam is the highest-fidelity capture route among the remake platforms.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Steam version on Windows with current patches. Use the separate Secret of Mana entry for the original SNES/Collection version.

entries.remaster_caveats: The remake changes the presentation and is not treated as a substitute for the original SNES/Collection route.

entries.title: Trials of Mana (2020 remake)

primary.why: The 2020 remake fully rebuilds Trials of Mana in 3D with voiceover, remastered music, a post-ending episode, an ability system, and new classes; Windows is the highest-fidelity capture route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Steam/Windows version with current patches. Use the Collection of Mana entry for the original 2D Super Famicom version.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use the original Trials of Mana entry for the 1995 2D version and its original feel.

entries.title: Echoes of Mana

emulation.notes: No complete legal offline route is documented.

primary.why: Echoes of Mana was a mobile action RPG for Android and iOS; service ended in 2023, so the original mobile release is the only version to document.
primary.how_to_play: No current official play route exists after end of service. Treat as a historical archive entry unless Square Enix rereleases it.

entries.remaster_caveats: Service ended in 2023, so this is not a current-play recommendation.

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native PC output with max settings.

primary.why: Visions of Mana is the 2024 mainline action RPG; Windows is the highest-fidelity and most capture-flexible route among the simultaneous PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC releases.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Steam or Microsoft Store Windows version with current patches and max settings. Use PS5 or Xbox Series X only if console capture is preferred.
